This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #48026
* #48025
* #48024
* #48023
* #48022
* #48021
* #48020
* __->__ #48019
* #48018
* #48017
* #48016
* #48015
* #48014
* #48013
* #48012
* #48011
* #48010
* #48009
* #48008
* #48007
* #48006
* #48005
* #48004
* #48003
* #48002
* #48001

## Motivation

Code outside the KV storage read the storage plan's lifetimes, the allocator's bands and id spaces directly (the Triton backend took window lengths and value widths from the plan; decode named host pools and tree slots through the plan and window bands; the PD setup branched on the storage's type), and a sub-pool's internal name crossed two external boundaries directly: PD peers ordered and compared window entries by it, and window usage metrics were labelled by it. Renaming a sub-pool inside the process would then change the transfer protocol and the metric series.

## Modifications

- `mem_cache/kv/storage.py`, `static_kv_storage.py`: thin storage methods answer what consumers need (`primary_window_name`, `host_pool_name`, `window_tree_component`, `entry_sub_pool`, `storage_format_tag`, `draft_hosting_sub_pools`, `holds_view`); the static storage answers the same calls (its one window, its window host pool, the window slot).
- `kv/router.py`, `kv/routed_cache.py`, `layers/attention/triton_backend.py`: a layer's route and its sub-pool carry the attention window it reads over; the Triton backend reads window lengths from its router and value widths from the views.
- `kv/plan.py`: the target's window is chosen by one rule (`primary_window`), shared by the plan and the sizing that runs before a plan exists. `available_units` is the planner's answer (the separate `device_room` read is removed), so a host load evicts only what a take cannot otherwise get.
- `kv/decl.py`, `disaggregation/utils.py`, `base/conn.py`, `decode.py`: `SubPoolExternal` declares a sub-pool's PD entry key and usage label (`wire_key`, `label`) beside its host pool and tree component names; wire entries carry their key (`WireEntry.key`), peers order and compare entries by it (`KVArgs.state_wire_keys`), and usage reports each sub-pool under its label. Static pools register no key.
- `managers/scheduler.py`: the window capacities in `/server_info` and the startup gauge are the storage's own figures (the denominators of the window usage gauges) instead of the one sizing token count every window was assigned.
- `hybrid_pool_assembler.py`, `base_prefix_cache.py`: the host-stack assembler builds its slot ids from the storage's tree slots.
- Tests: `test_unified_window_lengths.py`, `test_unified_window_wire.py`, `test_unified_window_sub_pools.py`.

**Behavior change:** `/server_info` `memory_usage.token_capacity_window` and `sglang:max_total_num_tokens_window` now report each window's own capacity from the storage. Wire keys and labels keep the names the previous PRs introduced, so PD pairing and metric names do not change here.

## Accuracy Tests

Serving validation was run at the **top of this 26-PR stack** (the cumulative change), not at this PR's head. Software: torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GSM8K is few-shot, 500 or 1319 questions as noted; `main` is the same commit the stack is based on, same flags.

| Hardware | Model | Configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, `--enable-unified-memory` (rebased stack) | 0.954 (1319 q) | 0.950–0.954 |
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP1, `--enable-unified-memory --max-total-tokens 120000` (rebased stack) | 0.842 (1319 q) | 0.839 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, MTP (EAGLE, 3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens) | 0.951, accept length 3.56 | 0.953, 3.56 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, DFlash draft | 0.951, accept length 5.42 | 0.952, 5.44 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PD (prefill TP1 + decode TP1, mooncake), unified, repeated runs | 0.952–0.960, no hang | 0.954–0.958 |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | PD (TP1 + TP1, mooncake), unified | 0.810 | 0.808 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, HiCache | 0.954 | — |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PP2, unified | 0.953 | 0.955 (static pools) |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified (500 q) | 0.958 | 0.960 |
| 2x B200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified, `trtllm_mha` (1319 q) | 0.849 | 0.863 |
| 2x B300 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B / openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified | 0.950 / 0.849 | 0.954 / 0.849 |

On B200 and B300, 40 greedy GSM8K generations were compared with `main`: 35–40 of 40 are identical, and the rest first differ after at least 27 characters (near ties). The H200 runs above other than the two marked "rebased stack" were run at the stack top before it was rebased onto the current base; the code they cover is unchanged by the rebase except for conflict resolutions.

Every serving row above reads sub-pool facts through these storage methods; the Triton path is covered by the unit tests in this stack.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Storage methods are thin lookups; no hot-path change intended. Measured at the stack top, same flags as `main` (bench_serving, random 4096-in / 512-out unless noted):

| Hardware | Model / configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b, unified, `--max-total-tokens 120000` | 3.93–3.95 req/s | 3.95 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B PD (TP1 + TP1), 2048-in / 256-out | 5.65–6.28 req/s | 6.21–6.29 req/s |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b PD (TP1 + TP1) | 9.39–9.45 req/s | 9.21 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B MTP TP2 / DFlash TP2 | 4.26 / 4.36 req/s | 4.29 / 4.35 req/s |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B TP2 / openai/gpt-oss-120b TP2 | 6.35 / 19.31 req/s | 6.34 / 19.28 req/s |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
